text:
maya: quick q — we're seeing sporadic helm upgrades fail when envFrom references a Secret created by terraform in a different pipeline. sometimes the secret exists, sometimes helm errors with \"secret not found\" during upgrade. anyone have a robust pattern to avoid the race?

sam: does the chart require the secret for startup? can you make it optional in the pod spec?

maya: it's used for a few DB creds that the app can fall back to env defaults for in dev, but prod needs it. code currently has:
```yaml
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.appSecret.name }}
```
which fails if terraform hasn't applied yet.

jon: two options I usually reach for: 1) guard in the helm template with `lookup` so envFrom is only rendered if the Secret exists, or 2) use `optional: true` on the secretRef and surface a clear startup error if values are missing.

sam: example `lookup` guard (helm 3.7+):
```gotpl
{{- $name := .Values.appSecret.name }}
{{- if and $name (lookup \"v1\" \"Secret\" .Release.Namespace $name) }}
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ $name | quote }}
{{- end }}
```
that prevents helm from rendering the envFrom when the secret isn't present.

maya: ooh. good. does `lookup` also work during `helm template` in CI? we rely on `helm template` checks in the deploy pipeline.

jon: `lookup` talks to the cluster, so `helm template` locally (no cluster) will return nil. your CI that does `helm template --validate` probably won't get the same behavior unless it's connected to a test cluster. for pure static templating you can still guard by checking the value string: `if .Values.appSecret.name` — but that doesn't detect the actual resource.

alex: another pragmatic pattern: render the secretRef with `optional: true` (k8s supports it on SecretRef) so the pod won't crash during manifest apply, and add a liveness/startup check in the app that fails fast in prod if creds are missing. example:
```yaml
envFrom:
- secretRef:
    name: {{ .Values.appSecret.name | quote }}
    optional: true
```
Then combine with a release policy: make prod rollout depend on terraform apply job that creates the secret.

maya: is `optional: true` widely supported? we run on GKE and EKS.

sam: yes, it's been supported for a while (k8s >= 1.17+). but watch out: `optional: true` only defers the missing-secret error to the runtime (the container may still fail if it needs the vars).

deploy-bot: latest prod canary failed: attach logs -> \"envFrom secret not found: my-app-prod-secret\" (2026-02-28T14:12:03Z) :warning:

jon: if you want strict behavior in prod, add a pre-install Helm hook job that waits for the secret (or validates terraform run). quick hook snippet: 
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: {{ include \"fullname\" . }}-wait-secret
  annotations:
    \"helm.sh/hook\": pre-install,pre-upgrade
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: wait-for-secret
        image: bitnami/kubectl:latest
        command: [\"/bin/sh\",\"-c\",\"until kubectl get secret -n {{ .Release.Namespace }} {{ .Values.appSecret.name }}; do sleep 2; done\"]
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
```
This blocks the release until the secret exists (but adds complexity).

maya: I like optional:true + pre-install hook for prod. for dev/staging we can keep it relaxed. any gotchas with helm hooks here?

sam: hooks bypass normal release ordering a bit and are harder to clean up on failures. also they run in the cluster, so your CI runner needs RBAC to list/get secrets. Use sparingly.

alex: another pattern: move secret creation into the same pipeline as the chart (i.e., terraform step runs before helm apply) and use `terraform apply && helm upgrade --install` in one job — simple and deterministic.

maya: thanks — plan: add `optional: true` to the envFrom, add a `lookup` guard in the chart (cluster-aware), and change prod pipeline to run terraform first + lightweight pre-install hook as a belt-and-suspenders check. I'll open a small PR with the template changes and ping infra for pipeline ordering.

sam: ping me on the PR, I'll quick-review. :thumbsup:

jon: one more small thing — for `helm template` checks in CI, you can add a fast unit test that runs the template with a fake secret name and asserts the rendered manifest contains `optional: true` when in prod values. that avoids false negatives.

maya: good call. I'll add that to the PR. thanks all!
